_note: Curated fixture evidence for the seeded VEGF-A demo. The citations point at real public records (UniProt, RCSB PDB, Drugs@FDA, ClinicalTrials.gov). They were assembled by hand for the demo, NOT retrieved by a live Paperclip call — every item's provenance records mode='fixture' and the UI labels it. Nothing here is a model-generated claim.

items.claim: VEGF-A (UniProt P15692) is a secreted, disulfide-linked homodimeric growth factor with a cystine-knot fold; the mature signalling unit is the dimer, not the monomer.
items.citation_locator: P15692, Function and Subunit structure sections

items.claim: The VEGFR-binding determinants sit at the two poles of the VEGF-A dimer and are formed by residues contributed by both protomers, so a binder targeting that region engages a composite surface rather than a single chain.
items.source_title: Wiesmann et al., Crystal structure at 1.7 A resolution of VEGF in complex with domain 2 of the Flt-1 receptor (Cell, 1997)

items.claim: A neutralising antibody Fab has been co-crystallised with VEGF-A, giving an experimentally determined blocking epitope that overlaps the receptor-binding region.
items.source_title: Muller et al., VEGF and the Fab fragment of a humanized neutralizing antibody: crystal structure of the complex and mutational analysis of the interface (Structure, 1998)

items.claim: VEGF-A is alternatively spliced into isoforms of differing length (commonly VEGF121, VEGF165, VEGF189). The heparin-binding exon 6/7 material is absent from VEGF121.
Anti-VEGF-A blockade is a clinically validated mechanism: bevacizumab (full-length IgG) and ranibizumab (Fab) are both approved and both act by sequestering VEGF-A.
items.source_title: Drugs@FDA approved product records for bevacizumab and ranibizumab

items.claim: The FDA withdrew the metastatic breast cancer indication for bevacizumab in 2011 after confirmatory trials failed to show a survival benefit. Target engagement is not the same thing as clinical benefit, and this target has a documented history of the two coming apart.
items.source_title: FDA decision withdrawing the metastatic breast cancer indication for bevacizumab (2011)

items.claim: Single-domain VHH (nanobody) therapeutics are a viable clinical format; caplacizumab was approved as the first nanobody-based medicine.
items.source_title: Drugs@FDA approved product record for caplacizumab

items.claim: Anti-VEGF agents remain under active clinical investigation across ophthalmology and oncology, indicating a live competitive landscape rather than an unexplored target.
items.source_title: ClinicalTrials.gov registered studies for VEGF-A-directed agents

items.claim: The VEGF-A monomer carries an intrachain cystine knot plus two inter-chain disulfides. Engineered binders that introduce free cysteines risk scrambling with this system during expression.
VEGF family members PlGF, VEGF-B, VEGF-C and VEGF-D share the cystine-knot fold with VEGF-A, so cross-reactivity against family members is a real selectivity risk for a new binder.
items.source_title: UniProtKB family and domain annotations for the PDGF/VEGF growth factor family

items.claim: Public co-structures of VEGF-A with both a receptor domain and a neutralising Fab give two independent experimental reference frames for scoring a predicted epitope.
No experimental binding, expression, or stability data exists for any candidate in this run. Every candidate-level number in this investigation is a computational prediction.
